speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) how will the Government assist residents who are not digitally literate with the use of digital services; and (b) how do Government agencies communicate with residents who do not have an email.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Additionally, many agencies provide in-person and contact centre services, to assist those who may have difficulty transacting with Government online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While the Government’s use of digital communication channels has increased, offline channels remain critical.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, the Silver Generation Office conducts outreach to communicate Government policies to residents and guide seniors who need help applying for assistance schemes online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even as more services are digitalised, the Government remains committed to maintaining an inclusive society and will continue to ensure that residents can communicate and transact with the Government, regardless of their digital ability.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I recently had a case where a resident wanted to file a complaint with the Community Dispute Resolution Tribunal (CDRT).

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: He had to navigate through the entire digital process when he needed to lodge a complaint.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, I asked one of my volunteers to help him.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: At the end of the day, my volunteer said the Court would then communicate with him via email.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: My resident tried to go to Court and the services rendered were not quite there.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We recognise that there will be situations like these where residents will feel quite unsure about what to do when they encounter Government services that have shifted online substantially.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: My suggestion to the Member is to encourage the resident to call at one of our ServiceSG Centres.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If all else fails, Mr Lim is very welcome to send an email to me and I will certainly find a way to help his resident.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have a very similar case where an elderly resident who has difficulty trying to file a claim to CDRT.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is, indeed, the philosophy that we are trying to adopt.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One very common reference that we can all relate to is the use of the CDC vouchers, for example.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Even in terms of how it is being designed, it has in mind how citizens who are not so comfortable using digital tools can be enabled to benefit from the scheme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is why a non-digital option was retained.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Over time, I think we see that fewer and fewer of our citizens need to rely on those non-digital options, but we will, obviously, have to keep those non-digital options available until such time that most, if not all, of these citizens can migrate to the digital versions.
